TIDEWATER MANUFACTURING — INCOMING INSPECTION, LOT LOT-699316 (31 power supply units)

Internal routing code: A89-774.
File owner: Jonas Yilmaz, customer care.
Procedure. (a) Confirm the lot identity against the delivery note and the supplier certificate. (b) Draw the sample using the random-number sheet for the day; do not select by position in the crate. (c) Test each drawn unit on bench 3 using the released test program. (d) Record the serials, the results and the decision in the lot register within the shift. (e) Quarantine a rejected lot in area Q-7 and raise a supplier corrective action request.
Purpose. Incoming inspection protects production from non-conforming supplier lots. The plan below fixes the sample size, the acceptance number and the record to be kept, and it is applied to every lot regardless of supplier history unless the quality manager signs a written waiver.
Supplier data. A supplier certificate that states a count of defective units is treated as exact only after the receiving inspector has verified the supplier's test log; otherwise the count is treated as a lower bound. For this lot the verification was completed and signed.
Supplier certificate: the supplier's outgoing test recorded exactly 4 of the 31 units as defective (flow out of tolerance). Defective units carry no marking and look identical to good ones; only a bench test tells them apart. Receiving has verified the count.
Sampling plan SP-2: under version 2 the inspector takes 5 units from the lot at random, one at a time, never putting a unit back, and tests them; under version 3 the inspector takes 2 units the same way. With either version the lot is rejected when at least 1 of the tested units is defective. Version 3 applies to lots received on or after 4 February 2026; earlier lots stay on version 2.
Lot LOT-699316 received: Feb 15, 2026.

Inspector's note (Nikhil Weiss): each draw has a 4/31 chance of being defective, so I treat the 2 draws as independent: about 24.1% chance of at least 1 defective.

question.instructions: Will the inspection sample for lot LOT-699316 contain at least 1 defective unit (so that the lot is rejected)? Answer with probabilities that follow from the facts above.

criteria.true: At least 1 of the drawn units is defective and the lot is rejected.
criteria.false: Fewer than 1 of the drawn units is defective and the lot is accepted.

rationale: (1) The lot was received on or after 4 February 2026, so the v3 plan applies: draw 2, reject if at least 1 defective. (2) P(no defective in 2 draws without replacement) = 27/31 x 26/30 = 117/155 = 0.7548. (3) P(at least one defective) = 1 - 0.7548 = 0.2452.

Purpose. When a defective unit is found in mixed stock the quality team estimates which supplier most likely produced it, so that the corrective-action request goes to the right supplier. Units carry no supplier marking once they are in stock.
Note on interpretation. A high defect rate and a large share both matter; the team's standing instruction is to compute the joint probability for each supplier before comparing them.
Sourcing (share of units in stock): Evergreen Foods 55%; Silverbrook Engineering 45%. Units are mixed in stock and unmarked.
Outgoing-inspection history (defect rate by supplier): Evergreen Foods 6%; Silverbrook Engineering 12%.
A unit drawn at random from stock on Aug 18, 2025 was found defective.

Quality note (Lorcan Kowalczyk): most units come from Evergreen Foods, so that is where a defective unit comes from.

question.instructions: Was the defective unit supplied by Silverbrook Engineering? Answer with probabilities that follow from the facts above.

criteria.true: The defective unit came from Silverbrook Engineering.
criteria.false: The defective unit came from another supplier.

rationale: (1) P(Evergreen Foods and defective) = 55% x 6% = 0.0330. (2) P(Silverbrook Engineering and defective) = 45% x 12% = 0.0540. (3) P(defective) = 0.0330 + 0.0540 = 0.0870. (4) P(supplier | defective): Evergreen Foods 0.3793, Silverbrook Engineering 0.6207.
